note: Single source of truth for the ALISA camera lexicon. Distilled from camera_slerp_director_studio.html but expressed SUBJECT-RELATIVE so any scene applies a shot regardless of scale. A shot = framing x angle x move. The Camera engine (World/Engines/Camera.py) resolves (framing, angle) against a subject {center:[x,y,z], height} into {pos, look, fov, roll}; moves are hints the JS runtime animates. Both the Python engine and the browser scenes read THIS file — do not hardcode shots per scene.

eyes.desc: anime reaction shot - just the eyes

low.desc: contrapicado - power/threat, looks up at subject

fisheye.desc: anime yandere fisheye - unhinged intensity, warped close

hero.desc: anime hero contrapicado - power, resolve, standing tall

dolly_zoom.desc: vertigo - dolly out while FOV compresses (or in/expand)

pull_out.desc: slow reveal away from the subject

snap_in.desc: anime impact - a hard snap-zoom onto the subject (the realization hits)

confesion_dramatica.desc: a heavy admission - power creeps in

revelacion.desc: the moment of truth in the eyes

establecer.desc: set the room before the scene

anime_reaccion.desc: ANIME: the reaction shot - cut to just the eyes on a beat of shock/realisation

anime_impacto.desc: ANIME: the impact - a hard snap-zoom when the truth lands

anime_yandere.desc: ANIME: warped fisheye intensity - the unhinged/obsessive beat

anime_heroe.desc: ANIME: the hero contrapicado - resolve, standing tall as the camera reveals

anime_tension.desc: ANIME: canted tension - something is deeply wrong
